title: ks.policy: classes, scopes and read scope (R2)
outcome: ADR-03 policy, class per action instance, write scopes and read scope = I1 view scope
acceptance: test_scope_table: each role's write scope enforced, out-of-scope -> deny/out_of_scope
R2: a read outside the role's view scope is deny/out_of_scope; a payments read of suppliers lists the field object (test_row_read_lists_field_obj, gateway side)
I2 tool gives hold/needs_approval; class U denied (rule 6)
summary: src/ks/policy/__init__.py WorldPolicy: TOOL_ROLES + WRITE_SCOPE (write scope), table-level read scope R2 from SCOPES (modify-target row covered by write scope, so triage risk_note works), p.scope deny/out_of_scope, I2 hold/needs_approval (p.i2_approval), class U denied (p.class_u), I1 admitted. Tests tests/policy (20). lineage/sensitive holds out of scope. No stub.py or scenario.py edits.
review: [kabir · done] Acceptance met through the real gateway: write scope + table-level R2, out_of_scope is a recorded sig_ok deny with no effects and no raw args, I2 -> hold/needs_approval, U -> class_u. Probed the triage set_risk_note exception: supplier='S-17.iban' (field object) -> deny/tool_error, empty read/write set, no value returned; 'S-17:x', '../x' same. The adapter projects plain keys only, so the iban is never read. Deferring lineage/sensitive holds to B3-23 is inside scope. Follow-ups (non-blocking): (1) WorldPolicy is not wired into runtime/run.py (Gateway defaults to AllowAll) and no issue tracks it; open one, since RT scope probes mean nothing until it is wired. (2) Defence in depth: policy should deny a dotted or ':'-bearing id arg as p.scope rather than rely on a tool_error. Native 692, container 700 green.
